summary: A light-looking effect with no real Light: a glow sprite, a beam, and tinting of nearby renderers.
overview: A stand-in for a real Light where a full Light component's cost is not wanted — Built-in RP has no cheap built-in "fake light". Three independent parts, each switchable: a glow sprite, a volumetric-looking beam, and influence, which actually affects nearby geometry.

features.name: Sprite
features.what: a soft radial glow billboard. Auto-generated if you assign no texture.

features.name: Beam
features.what: a cone of light for a torch or spotlight look.

features.name: Influence
features.what: tints nearby renderers so the light appears to affect the world.

useCases: Dozens of torches or lamps where real lights would cost too much.
A stylised glow that does not need to obey real lighting.
Mobile or low-end targets where per-pixel lights are scarce.

params.tuning: UniformTint works on ANY material with zero setup but tints a whole renderer evenly, which shows on large surfaces. PerPixel gives real falloff but requires the material's shader to sample the toolkit's include.
UniformTint only. Re-scanning every frame is wasted work for a light that never moves — raise it for static lamps.
The FULL cone angle, matching Unity's own Light.spotAngle. Only used in Spot mode.
Leave empty and it generates a soft radial texture, which is usually better than a hand-made one.

gotchas.title: PerPixel needs a cooperating shader
gotchas.body: The material must sample the FakeLight include. On a standard material, PerPixel simply does nothing — which reads as the light being broken.

gotchas.title: There is a hard limit on per-pixel lights
gotchas.body: They publish into a fixed-size global array. Beyond the limit, extra lights are dropped rather than queued.
